newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania police start crackdown on criminal gangs.
newsitem.headline: Albania police start crackdown on criminal gangs.

text.p: Albanian police will launch a major drive this week to restore order in the Balkan country after months of anarchy, the Interior Ministry said on Monday.
The ministry urged Albanians to back police in their campaign to fight armed gangs, unblock main roads and return peace and order to the nation.
"The police, determined to act firmly...against armed criminals, call on all citizens to back their operations and give them moral support," ministry spokesman Ndrek Gjini told Reuters.

More than 1,500 people have been killed in the former communist country since violence, looting and chaos broke out in March after thousands of Albanians lost their life savings when a string of corrupt pyramid investment schemes collapsed.
Gjini said some 60 people were killed last week and another 100 injured in shooting incidents. Around one million looted guns are believed to be still in circulation.

The Albanian news agency ATA said Deputy Interior Minister Sokol Bare had ordered police to take control of main roads linking Tirana with the rest of the country and speed up action against armed gangs.
"Make no mistake, there will be no compromise with those who are terrorising, looting and killing innocent people," he said.

The violence brought down the Democratic Party government and led to early elections in June in which the Democrats lost heavily to the Socialists. The result also led to the downfall of ex-president Sali Berisha, who resigned last month.
Socialist Prime Minister Fatos Nano has made clear his government's priority is to restore order as soon as possible.

Interior Minister Neritan Ceka said last week that police had destroyed seven armed bands so far and would soon turn their efforts to the southern towns of Vlore, Gjirokaster and Berat, main centres of unrest and lawlessness.
On Sunday police arrested four masked men in Gjirokaster, 232 km (145 miles) south of Tirana, on charges of robbing locals and businessmen, many of them from Greece.
One of those arrested was a policeman who had joined the gang last month.
A Gjirokaster resident told Reuters by telephone that the townspeople welcomed the police action and were keen to rid the area of criminal bands.
